findings_table.title: unhandled asynchronous ChildProcess 'error' kills the launcher past the transfer point of no return
findings_table.line: 469-476 (spawn with no child 'error' listener); 487 registers a listener on the stdio stream only
supporting_lines: tools/terminal0/lrcq/run-five-hour.mjs:495 (.catch handles promise rejections, not EventEmitter 'error' events)
findings_table.mechanism: child_process.spawn reports spawn failures ASYNCHRONOUSLY, by emitting 'error' on the returned ChildProcess. The try/catch wrapping spawn() catches only synchronous throws (invalid argument types). No child.on('error') / child.once('error') is ever registered — only writer.on('error') on the fd-3 stream, a different EventEmitter — and neither the authority module nor the launcher installs a process-level uncaughtException handler. An actual spawn failure therefore raises an unhandled 'error' event after the key has been exported, the frame encoded, the key deleted from module storage and the capability marked TRANSFERRED_SPENT.
findings_table.reproduction: Two independent triggers, each in a disposable world with a genuine CONSUMED capability and a valid signed launch intent. (1) pass cwd pointing at a non-existent directory; (2) make process.execPath unreachable, modelling the node binary this run was launched with being removed or renamed mid-run — on this host node lives under ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.1, so an nvm version removal during a five-hour run does exactly this. Both: `node p3-d2.mjs` -> "node:events:486 throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event ... Error: spawn <path> ENOENT", exit 1. Control run with no patch: returns OK, 1 child, exit 0. With an uncaughtException handler artificially installed to absorb the event, the function is observed to return TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED in ~1ms.
findings_table.actual_result: The launcher process terminates with exit 1 and a raw stack trace. launchDetachedSupervisorV4 never returns its structured { final_state: 'SUPERVISOR_SPAWN_FAILED' } refusal, its `finally { closeSync(outFd); closeSync(errFd) }` never runs, and no truthful evidence record of the failure is produced — at the single most sensitive point in the authority chain, immediately after the founder authorization has been irreversibly consumed.
findings_table.required_secure_result: spawnGovernedSupervisorV4 must register child.once('error', ...) synchronously, before the first await, race it against the descriptor write, kill and reap any partial child, and RETURN { ok: false, code: TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED, transfer: TRANSFERRED_SPENT } so the launcher can record the truthful refusal and exit cleanly.
findings_table.zero_spawn_status: MET — 0 productive-provider spawns, 0 key frames delivered, 0 children that ran, 0 claims, retry ALREADY_TRANSFERRED. This is not an authority bypass: no second process ever receives the key and the capability is correctly unusable afterwards.
findings_table.narrow_correction_scope: One child.once('error') registration inside spawnGovernedSupervisorV4 plus a call to the existing killAndReap, and one regression test in checker-197-corrections.selftest.mjs. No other file changes.
findings_table.claim_accuracy_note: The correction ledger asserts for FG-CHK-197-01 that 'killAndReap kills AND reaps a partially launched child on transfer failure' and that the post-materialization failure path is corrected. The transfer-failure path is only covered for a descriptor WRITE failure, not for a spawn failure; the corrections family's own comment at checker-197-corrections.selftest.mjs:84-85 concedes no descriptor-failure case could be constructed, so no test exercises either variant.

findings_table.title: the productive-provider spawn boundary enforces no ceiling on the founder-signed limits and does not require all signed exclusions
findings_table.line: 53-64 (limits: presence and positivity only, compared to nothing); 108 (must-be-true list omits no_deploy and no_push_unless_authorized)
findings_table.mechanism: Three gaps compose. (1) projectionMatchesCapability binds a projection to a capability by authoritative===false, projection_schema, v4_supervisor_claim_digest and v4_activation_identity ONLY — never by any limit or exclusion field. (2) validateActivation requires max_budget_usd, per_job_timeout_s, max_parallel_width, max_output_bytes and termination_grace_s to be present, finite and positive, but compares them to nothing; no code path anywhere re-derives the signed limits for comparison at the boundary. (3) no_deploy appears in neither REQUIRED_FIELDS nor the must-be-true list, and no_push_unless_authorized is presence-checked only and absent from the must-be-true list at line 108 — false is not undefined/null/'' so it passes the presence check.
findings_table.reproduction: From inside a genuine detached supervisor holding a genuine SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capability, hand runJob a spread copy of the honest projection with one field changed, using a provider stub that appends to a log on every execution. 6 of 26 invalid routes spawned it: max_budget_usd 10->1000; per_job_timeout_s 2700->999999; max_parallel_width 2->64; max_output_bytes 10485760->1e12; no_deploy true->false; no_push_unless_authorized true->false. A second pass with a stub that records its own argv proved the widened value reaches the provider: 'SPAWNED max-budget-usd=1000' (honest control: 'SPAWNED max-budget-usd=10').
findings_table.actual_result: The productive provider is spawned, and --max-budget-usd — the single money control handed to the real Claude CLI for a five-hour paid run — is whatever the record says. per_job_timeout_s becomes the kill timer and max_output_bytes the overflow ceiling, so both bounds are equally unenforced. Two founder-signed exclusions can be dropped without refusal.
findings_table.required_secure_result: Zero productive-provider spawn for every one of these routes. The boundary must (a) require all ten signed exclusions to be true, and (b) compare every limit against an immutable reference re-derived from the signed activation, refusing any record that widens one.
findings_table.zero_spawn_status: NOT MET — 6 productive-provider spawns across the 26 invalid routes. The review contract's Phase 9 requirement ('wrong deadline, budget, timeout, width, output limit, or exclusion ... require zero productive-provider spawn for every invalid route') fails for budget, timeout, width, output limit and exclusions. Deadline is correctly refused.
findings_table.narrow_correction_scope: Add no_deploy, no_push_unless_authorized and no_external_comms to the must-be-true list in activation-schema.mjs:108, and add limit-ceiling comparisons at the real-provider boundary against a reference re-derived from the signed activation (NOT from cap.limits — see FG-FCHK-197-C, or the reference is itself mutable). Extend projectionMatchesCapability to cover the limit and exclusion fields.
findings_table.exploitability_note: Reachable only by code running inside the supervisor process, i.e. the same in-process threat model that FG-CHK-197-06 was accepted at LOW under. Rated MEDIUM because the control defeated is the run's cost ceiling and two founder exclusions, and because the contract's mechanical requirement is unambiguous.

findings_table.title: nested limits/exclusions objects escape the shallow freeze on the VERIFIED and SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capabilities — the same defect class FG-CHK-197-06 claimed closed
findings_table.line: 98 (makeCapability does a shallow Object.freeze); 181 (limits: a plain object literal); 182 (exclusions: a plain object literal)
supporting_lines: src/v8b/lrcq/assurance/lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs:319 (limits copied BY REFERENCE onto the SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capability)
src/v8b/lrcq/run-harness/v4-legacy-projection.mjs:58-62 (narrow() treats cap.limits as the signed ceiling)
findings_table.mechanism: Object.freeze is shallow. FG-CHK-197-06 was closed by moving __state off the CONSUMED capability into a module-private WeakMap, but limits and exclusions remain plain nested object literals on the VERIFIED capability, and limits is copied by reference onto the SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capability. Any holder of either capability can write to them, and every downstream consumer treats them as the authoritative founder-signed ceiling.
findings_table.reproduction: On the genuine, frozen, module-branded SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capability obtained through the full real route: cap.limits.max_budget_usd = 777777; cap.limits.max_parallel_width = 99 — both writes take effect. The GENUINE projectLegacyActivationV4 then produced a frozen, authoritative:false projection with max_budget_usd: 777777 that projectionMatchesCapability ACCEPTED, and the recording stub logged 'SPAWNED max-budget-usd=777777'. On the VERIFIED capability: max_budget_usd 10->999999, run_duration_s 18000->99999999, max_parallel_width 2->64, exclusions.no_deploy true->false, exclusions.no_live_action true->false.
findings_table.actual_result: Reflect.ownKeys probing reports nested_MUTABLE_object_properties: ['limits','exclusions'] on VERIFIED and ['limits'] on SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION. The founder-signed cost ceiling, duration, parallel width, output cap and grace period are all mutable, and no record tampering is needed to widen the provider's actual --max-budget-usd.
findings_table.required_secure_result: Deep-freeze (or return a fresh frozen clone on read) every nested object on all three capability stages, so nested_mutable_objects === 0 for VERIFIED, CONSUMED and SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION.
findings_table.zero_spawn_status: NOT MET — composite with FG-FCHK-197-B: this route produced a productive-provider spawn under a widened signed budget via a fully genuine projection. Note both fixes are required: deep-freezing alone leaves the hand-widened-record route open, and boundary enforcement alone is defeated if its reference is cap.limits.
findings_table.narrow_correction_scope: One deepFreeze helper applied in makeCapability (activation-v4.mjs:98) and at the SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION mint (lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs:315-333), plus extending C6d in checker-197-corrections.selftest.mjs to probe all three stages rather than only CONSUMED.
findings_table.claim_accuracy_note: The correction ledger's result_after for FG-CHK-197-06 asserts nested_mutable_objects: 0 and own_keys_with_mutable_state: 0. Both are false for the VERIFIED and SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capabilities. The regression assertion C6d probes only the CONSUMED capability, whose own property values are all strings, so it cannot detect this.
findings_table.additional_observation: cap.exclusions is a hardcoded three-field object { no_deploy, no_push_unless_authorized, no_live_action } rather than a projection of the ten signed exclusion fields. Because the verifier already refuses any exclusion that is not true, the constant cannot misreport a signed false — but it is a redundant mutable copy of signed authority and should either derive from the payload or be removed.

findings_table.title: the FG-CHK-197-05 filesystem-object-identity gate is built but wired into no authority read; its refusal code is dead
findings_table.line: 45 (ROOT_OBJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH declared and never returned); 132 and 149 (both assertAuthorityObject calls omit expectObjectId)
supporting_lines: src/v8b/lrcq/assurance/lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs:190, 249-250 (the object id is RECORDED into the marker and intent but never checked against the live root)
findings_table.mechanism: The correction records lifecycle_root_object_id into the consumed marker and the launch intent and adds an expectObjectId parameter to assertAuthorityObject, but no production call site ever supplies it. Mechanical confirmation: expectObjectId appears at exactly one call site in the whole repository and it is inside checker-197-corrections.selftest.mjs:229; and of the 46 codes declared in LC_CODES only two are never referenced in the module body — TERMINAL and ROOT_OBJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH.
findings_table.reproduction: Consume an activation (the marker records dev:16777230/ino:106097623). Rename the lifecycle root aside and mkdir a fresh directory at the SAME path (dev:16777230/ino:106097629). Copy the marker and intent in at 0600. Attach: the result is KEY_MISMATCH — the attach proceeded past resolveSignedRoot and both readRecord calls to the cryptographic comparison, with no object-identity refusal anywhere.
findings_table.actual_result: The recorded lifecycle_root_object_id is inert: a different filesystem object at the signed path is not refused. The documented property 'a DIFFERENT filesystem object is refused even when its path string looks similar' holds only for a direct unit call that supplies expectObjectId, never on a production route.
findings_table.required_secure_result: resolveSignedRoot and readRecord must, on every authority read after the marker exists, pass expectObjectId derived from the marker's recorded lifecycle_root_object_id and return ROOT_OBJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH on a mismatch.
findings_table.zero_spawn_status: MET — 0 productive-provider spawns; the attack terminated at KEY_MISMATCH.
findings_table.narrow_correction_scope: Thread the marker's recorded object id into resolveSignedRoot/readRecord as expectObjectId at the two call sites, or delete the unused parameter and the dead code and correct the documented property. One regression test per branch.
findings_table.residual_risk_bound: Not remotely exploitable. A different local uid cannot stage records: the owner and mode guards refuse foreign-owned records, the lifecycle root is inside the repository at mode <= 0755 owned by the running user, and ROOT_ESCAPES_REPO confines it. A same-uid actor already holds equivalent authority.
findings_table.claim_accuracy_note: The ledger's wording ('assertAuthorityObject CAN require the SAME object at every later read') is honest. The V4_AUTHORITY_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX and the ledger result_after row 'different_filesystem_object_with_similar_path: FS_OBJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH' read as an achieved production property and should be qualified as a unit-level capability that is not yet wired.
findings_table.additional_observation: The supervisor claim body records no lifecycle_root_object_id. The Phase 6 requirement that the canonical device/inode identity remain consistent across marker, intent AND claim holds only transitively, through the signed consumed_marker_digest and launch_intent_digest the claim carries. That is equivalent cryptographic binding, but the claim itself does not record the property.

findings_table.title: two regression assertions do not test what their labels claim, and one ledger result_after is presented as achieved when it is untestable
findings_table.mechanism: C1i is labelled 'zero provider spawn during the attack (only the governed supervisor entrypoint ran)' but its predicate is receipts.every(r => r.read_error === null || r.frame_bytes === 0) — a statement about receipt fields that is satisfied whether or not a provider was spawned. Nothing in the C1 family counts provider spawns. C4h is labelled 'the guard compares owner against the running uid' but asserts only assertAuthorityObject(marker, SECRET_OR_MUTABLE).ok === true && statSync(marker).uid === process.getuid() — it shows a correctly-owned file passes and cannot show a wrongly-owned file fails. The ledger then lists owner_mismatch: 'RECORD_UNSAFE_OWNER / ROOT_UNSAFE_OWNER' among the achieved result_after values for FG-CHK-197-04, though producing an owner mismatch requires root.
findings_table.reproduction: Read the two assertion expressions against their labels. Independently: this Checker's own concurrent attack measured 0 productive-provider spawns directly, and confirmed the uid comparison line is present and correctly wired — so the underlying behaviour is sound; it is the evidence that overstates.
findings_table.actual_result: Two green assertions certify properties they do not measure, and one ledger row presents a source-proven property as a dynamically achieved result. On a regression family whose stated purpose is 'not merely no crash', this weakens the corrected candidate's evidence rather than its behaviour.
findings_table.required_secure_result: C1i must count actual provider spawns (e.g. a recording stub at the signed provider target, asserted to be zero). C4h must be relabelled to what it proves, with the uid comparison recorded as source-proven. The ledger's owner_mismatch row must be marked SOURCE-PROVEN (root required), not an achieved result.
findings_table.zero_spawn_status: n/a — an evidence-quality finding. The underlying properties were independently confirmed by this Checker.
findings_table.narrow_correction_scope: Two assertion bodies/labels in checker-197-corrections.selftest.mjs and one row in CHECKER_197_CORRECTION_LEDGER.json.
findings_table.related_observation: C3j, C3k, C3l, C3m, C7e, C7f, C9b and C9c are source-text regex assertions rather than executions; C3l in particular compares source string offsets, not execution order. C3n/C3o do supply a real behavioural end-to-end check for that family, and this Checker independently confirmed the execution order behaviourally, so these are noted for evidence hygiene rather than raised as defects.

observations_not_findings: machine-verifier-exec.mjs:18 runs the backlog's declared test commands through a PATH-resolved allowlist [node, npm, git, shasum]. Its own repository observations (branch, diff --name-only, diff --numstat) correctly use fixedGit. Running node/npm by name is inherent to executing declared test commands; `git` is the one allowlist entry for which a pinned path exists but is not used. Not an authority observation, so not raised as a finding.

verifyFixedExecutable checks regular/non-symlink/executable but not ownership. /usr/bin/git is root:wheel 0755 and /bin/ps is root:wheel 4755 on this SIP-protected volume, so a non-root user cannot substitute them. Adding a root-owner and no-group/other-write check would be a cheap hardening.
